description: We are Cypher Squad, a team of 2nd-year B.Tech students (Ahmedabad Event) building a secure health monitoring dashboard for astronauts. We combine Python, C, Java, and cybersecurity to create real-time vital telemetry with encrypted data privacy. Looking for UI/UX designers, ML enthusiasts, and frontend devs to join us!
summary: VitalOrbit is an offline-first, autonomous Crew Health Command Center built for long-duration deep-space missions where light-time communication delays of up to 20 minutes prevent real-time Earth telemedicine. Grounded in NASA's 5 Hazards of Human Spaceflight and Canadian Space Agency (CSA) radiation monitoring frameworks, VitalOrbit combines a 3-second fleet triage roster, an interactive anatomical heat-map, 21-day personal baseline z-score anomaly detection, and behavioural vigilance tools—empowering astronauts and onboard Flight Surgeons to detect physiological or psychological risks early and execute explainable countermeasures autonomously.
details:
The Challenge

During a 500-Sol Mars transit, one-way light-time communication delays of up to 20 minutes and periodic blackouts make real-time ground medical supervision impossible. Simultaneously, microgravity induces physiological adaptations—such as resting bradycardia, cephalad fluid shifts, and bone/muscle loss—that cause false alarms under rigid terrestrial thresholds, while physical vitals, radiation dosimetry, and mental health are rarely integrated with crew privacy protections.

Our Solution

VitalOrbit is an autonomous, offline-first clinical command interface engineered for rapid triage under high-stress conditions, enabling fleet-wide assessment in 3 seconds and organ-level diagnostics in 2 clicks:

1. 3-Second Fleet Triage & Interactive Physiological Twin:

- A left-rail Crew Roster displays composite Health Score rings (0–100) with WCAG AA dual-coded icons and status labels (NOMINAL, WATCH, CRITICAL).

- Selecting any crew member updates a central interactive SVG human body heat-map across five systems: Cardiovascular, Musculoskeletal, Neuro-Vestibular, Sleep/Circadian, and Radiation.

2. Personal-Baseline Anomaly Engine & What-If Simulator:

- Rather than static ground cut-offs, VitalOrbit computes rolling 21-day personal z-scores (+σ) per astronaut.

- Every AI alert explains its contributing biometric signals, confidence score, 48-hour risk forecast, and actionable Flight Surgeon protocols.

- An interactive What-If Mission Simulator allows crew to test how sleep adjustments, ARED resistance workouts, EVA duration, and cabin CO2 partial pressure affect predicted readiness scores, paired with an offline natural-language medical query assistant.

3. Behavioural Health, Cognitive Vigilance & Granular Privacy:

- Includes a 30-second daily mood/stress/fatigue/motivation check-in, an interactive 5-second Psychomotor Vigilance Task (PVT) reaction-time micro-test, team interaction cohesion bars, and a guided 4-4-4-4 vagal-tone breathing pacer.

- Role-based access switches between Flight Surgeon, Astronaut (Personal), and Mission Control views. Astronauts control granular consent toggles that mask sensitive behavioural details from ground controllers while logging all record views in an immutable local audit trail.

4. Deep-Space Realism & Adaptive Cabin Display Modes:

- Simulates a 12m 40s one-way Earth communication delay in Autonomous Care Mode, queuing encrypted messages for downlink and generating printable PDF medical summary reports.

- Includes a 500-Sol Mission Timeline Scrubber (featuring historical replay of a Sol 199 Solar Particle Event and a guided 4-step "Trigger Demo Incident" walkthrough) plus Light Clinical, Mission Control Dark, and Red-Shift Night themes to preserve crew dark adaptation.

Technical Architecture & Verification

Built with React, TypeScript, Vite, Tailwind CSS v4, Recharts, Zustand, and browser IndexedDB for zero-network offline persistence, with automated unit tests in Vitest verifying the rolling z-score calculations and predictive scoring engine.

Space-to-Earth Impact

Beyond deep-space exploration, VitalOrbit's offline-first personal-baseline triage, low-burden cognitive screening, and privacy-preserving architecture directly translate to remote rural clinics, disaster-response teams, maritime vessels, and isolated polar expeditions on Earth.
